QuestInfo.name: The Faded Ink
QuestInfo.0: #b#p602##k is working on the ledger. I should see how far he's gotten.
QuestInfo.1: #b#p602##k rebound the ledger but couldn't restore one long entry. He sent me to the #b#p606##k, who keeps records of her own.
QuestInfo.2: The #b#p606##k couldn't decode the long entry at all. She directed me to #b#m010003000##k to speak with the #b#p411##k.

0.0: Rebound and set. It's a proper ledger again rather than a heap.
0.1: Most of it came back. I wasn't able to fully restore the long entry, but I did notice something strange about it. \nIt is not written like the others. The short ones are one visit each, done and closed. That one goes on for pages and never settles on anything.
0.2: I can't make sense of what's left of it, mind. It reads like a record and I am not a record-keeper. Shall I point you toward someone who is?

yes.0: Take it to the #b#p606##k at the #b#m010005001##k. She keeps a book much like this one.\nShe may see something in it that I can't.

no.0: Please return when you are ready.

1.0: You'd like me to examine this book? Of course! Please, set it here.
1.1: Oh, this is kept just like my own records. Though I don't know the handwriting.
1.2: Entry 88. Four minutes recorded. Came into the #b#m010003003##k, started downstairs, changed their mind and left.
1.3: Entry 91. One hour in the steam room. Never once touched the water. \nThose two are whole. Single entries, well kept. I have hundreds like them.
1.4: The long one is a bit confusing. It just goes on and on... \nAnd the style changes as it goes. Not the handwriting — that is the same throughout. The way they wrote changes. As if this was written over many years?
1.5: I keep records like this myself. Arrivals, rooms, dates, and a closing line when a guest leaves. That last part is most of the job.
1.6: There is no closing line anywhere in here. Not one. Whoever keeps this book has been writing people in for years and nobody has ever signed out.
1.7: What I can read of the long entry is #b#m010003000##k, and a name I did not expect. The #b#p411##k. Perhaps he can fill in the gaps. I'll go ahead and send it to him for you!

item.0: You'd like me to examine something? I'd be happy to, once you have it with you.

lost.0: You lost it? Luckily I made a duplicate while I was making repairs. Please be more careful with this one.
